sequence: Show the specific proposed edit and assumptions
Show water, energy, land and wider implications
Apply the prepared alternative or revise/reset
interaction.user_input_rule: Natural-language examples are intents, not a parser. A future language layer may select an ID/parameters; compute.py supplies numbers and constraints.
interaction.state_rule: Preview is separate from applying a design. Compare under the same baseline/rainfall. Navigate by loading complete states; replay never accumulates consumption.
interaction.unsupported_rule: Do not force batteries, new sites, new power plants or arbitrary cooling technologies into these four actions. Explain unsupported scope; request clarification when the goal does not identify a change.
interaction.combination_rule: One change per preview in this version. Do not sum savings across changes; solar/roof equipment, tank/hardstanding and operating water/energy interactions need a combined design model.

comparison_policy.mode: Alternative design from the same preconstruction baseline; not an operating-building retrofit.
comparison_policy.missing_values: null means Not established, never zero
comparison_policy.scores: No universal environmental or approval score

changes.title: Add rooftop solar
user_examples: Put solar panels on the roof.
Can solar cover 10% of our annual electricity?
changes.implementation: Reserve a roof zone, add ventilated PV racks and electrical integration; start generation at operation.
changes.why_interesting: Own generation reduces grid purchases while computing demand remains; roof space limits the target.
constraints: Prepared allocation is 6,000 m²; its actual fit is unknown.
Roof structure, cooling equipment, maintenance/fire access, local shading and interconnection require assessment.
Production is a regional long-term estimate, not measured Polo roof output.
No battery, night supply or peak-connection reduction is promised.
changes.visual: At M4 show a dashed solar zone; at M5 install panels; at M6 add a solar branch before the grid meter. Keep the IT/support demand unchanged.
changes.wider: Potentially lower annual electricity bought through the shared system. Grid capacity and neighbourhood outage effects remain unassessed.

changes.title: Keep a larger grass strip
user_examples: Keep more of the park green.
Use less hardstanding and preserve the grass.
changes.implementation: Exclude an additional original-turf strip from works and reduce proposed final non-roof hardstanding by the same area; keep roof and IT demand.
changes.why_interesting: A softer surface lowers modelled event runoff but the inherited irrigation allowance increases water demand.
constraints: Same 4 ha campus and 1.2 ha roof; replace proposed non-roof hardstanding only.
Delivery, emergency access, parking and utility layouts must still be resolved.
No automatic reduction in construction duration, machinery, materials or cooling demand.
The strip stays inside the campus; green area is not restored public playing space or a measured biodiversity gain.
changes.visual: Before M1 mark a protected strip and leave it intact through preparation. At opening reduce hardstanding accordingly; show the same buildings and a clear campus boundary.
changes.wider: The proposal retains more original turf but still occupies the same park footprint. Public access and community acceptance are not inferred.

changes.title: Improve cooling-water management
user_examples: Can we discharge less cooling water?
changes.implementation: Assume suitable treatment and conductivity/blowdown control permit a higher concentration ratio in the evaporative outdoor circuit.
changes.why_interesting: Less blowdown reduces make-up supply while the same heat-rejection evaporation remains.
constraints: The range 4–6 is a prepared teaching range, not a verified chemistry limit.
Feasibility at 6 requires water-quality and treatment assessment.
Keep evaporation and IT demand fixed for the conditional calculation; negligible drift/leaks.
Control/treatment electricity and any additional process water remain unquantified; no energy saving is invented.
changes.visual: At M5 add a schematic control/treatment marker. At M6 narrow make-up and blowdown arrows while keeping evaporation visible and unchanged; do not animate literal loop counts.
changes.wider: Conditionally lower cooling supply and sanitary blowdown. No drinking-water shortage, treatment-plant capacity relief or river outcome is calculated.
